programme.title: AWS Storage and Backup Follow Along
programme.outcome: Create and restore encrypted EBS storage from a snapshot; build encrypted Regional EFS across two Availability Zones with mount targets and an access point; select the correct Amazon FSx family; create an AWS Backup vault, plan, resource selection and EBS/EFS recovery points; choose S3 Glacier retrieval options and Storage Gateway architectures; and safely delete only resources created by the lab.
programme.statusNotice: Offline authoring manuscript only — not locally validated, imported, accepted, approved, published or fingerprinted.
completionDefinition: Two SSM-managed EC2 clients are created in eu-west-2a and eu-west-2b without SSH access.
A 4-GiB encrypted gp3 EBS volume is formatted, written, snapshotted and restored to a second encrypted volume.
The restored EBS volume contains the original training file and remains AZ-scoped to eu-west-2a.
An encrypted Regional EFS file system has one mount target in each client Availability Zone.
An EFS access point enforces /shared and POSIX identity 1001:1001; client B reads a file written by client A.
A complete Amazon FSx decision matrix distinguishes Windows File Server, Lustre, ONTAP and OpenZFS.
AWS Backup contains a scheduled plan/explicit resource selection plus completed on-demand EBS and EFS recovery points.
A complete S3 Glacier retrieval matrix covers Instant Retrieval, Flexible Retrieval Expedited/Standard/Bulk and Deep Archive Standard/Bulk without incurring archive minimum-duration lab charges.
A complete Storage Gateway architecture matrix covers S3 File Gateway, FSx File Gateway, cached/stored Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway.
All recovery points, storage, compute, networking, service roles, credentials and local files are removed in reverse dependency order.

editableBlocks.title: instance-user-data.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euxo pipefail

dnf install -y amazon-efs-utils xfsprogs

systemctl enable amazon-ssm-agent
systemctl start amazon-ssm-agent

editableBlocks.title: prepare-ebs.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_SOURCE=$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /)
ROOT_PARENT=$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$ROOT_SOURCE" | head -n1)

DATA_DEV=$(lsblk -dpno NAME,TYPE | awk '$2=="disk"{print $1}' | grep -v "/dev/${ROOT_PARENT}" | head -n1)

if [ -z "${DATA_DEV}" ]; then
  echo "No non-root EBS data disk was detected."
  exit 1
fi

sudo mkfs.xfs -f "${DATA_DEV}"
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ebs
sudo mount "${DATA_DEV}" /mnt/ebs

echo "fa-s3-storage encrypted EBS snapshot training file" | sudo tee /mnt/ebs/ebs-training.txt
sudo sync

sudo cat /mnt/ebs/ebs-training.txt
lsblk -f

editableBlocks.title: unmount-ebs.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

sudo sync
sudo umount /mnt/ebs

editableBlocks.title: verify-restored-ebs.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_SOURCE=$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /)
ROOT_PARENT=$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$ROOT_SOURCE" | head -n1)

DATA_DEV=$(lsblk -dpno NAME,TYPE | awk '$2=="disk"{print $1}' | grep -v "/dev/${ROOT_PARENT}" | head -n1)

if [ -z "${DATA_DEV}" ]; then
  echo "No restored non-root EBS data disk was detected."
  exit 1
fi

sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ebs-restored
sudo mount -o ro "${DATA_DEV}" /mnt/ebs-restored
sudo cat /mnt/ebs-restored/ebs-training.txt

tasks.title: Create the two-AZ VPC, security groups and service roles
tasks.goal: Create a dedicated VPC with two public subnets, no inbound EC2 access, NFS restricted from the EC2 SG to the EFS SG, an EC2 SSM role and an AWS Backup role.
tasks.whyItMatters: Two EC2 clients in different Availability Zones are needed to prove EFS shared access, while SSM avoids SSH keys/inbound SSH.
tasks.examRelevance: The network is deliberately minimal so the lab remains about storage rather than application networking.

browserSteps.instruction: Open VPC in eu-west-2.
Create fa-s3-storage-vpc with CIDR 10.130.0.0/16.
Create fa-s3-storage-public-a in eu-west-2a with 10.130.1.0/24.
Create fa-s3-storage-public-b in eu-west-2b with 10.130.2.0/24.
Enable auto-assign public IPv4 on both subnets.
Create fa-s3-storage-igw and attach it to the VPC.
Create fa-s3-storage-public-rt, add 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW, and associate both subnets.
Create fa-s3-storage-ec2-sg with no inbound rules and default outbound.
Create fa-s3-storage-efs-sg with inbound NFS TCP 2049 from fa-s3-storage-ec2-sg only.
Open IAM and create fa-s3-storage-ec2-role trusted by ec2.amazonaws.com.
Attach AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.
Create instance profile fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile and add the EC2 role.
Create fa-s3-storage-backup-role trusted by backup.amazonaws.com.
Attach AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create EC2 role
cliBlocks.content: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-s3-storage-ec2-role --assume-role-policy-document file://ec2-trust.json --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - add EC2 role
cliBlocks.content: aws iam add-role-to-instance-profile --instance-profile-name fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile --role-name fa-s3-storage-ec2-role --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create Backup role
cliBlocks.content: aws iam create-role --role-name fa-s3-storage-backup-role --assume-role-policy-document file://backup-trust.json --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create VPC
cliBlocks.content: $VPC_ID = aws ec2 create-vpc --cidr-block 10.130.0.0/16 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=vpc,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-vpc}]" --query Vpc.VpcId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - subnet A
cliBlocks.content: $SUBNET_A_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2a --cidr-block 10.130.1.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-public-a}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - subnet B
cliBlocks.content: $SUBNET_B_ID = aws ec2 create-subnet --vpc-id $VPC_ID --availability-zone eu-west-2b --cidr-block 10.130.2.0/24 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=subnet,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-public-b}]" --query Subnet.SubnetId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create IGW
cliBlocks.content: $IGW_ID = aws ec2 create-internet-gateway --tag-specifications "ResourceType=internet-gateway,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-igw}]" --query InternetGateway.InternetGatewayId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - route table
cliBlocks.content: $RT_ID = aws ec2 create-route-table --vpc-id $VPC_ID --tag-specifications "ResourceType=route-table,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-public-rt}]" --query RouteTable.RouteTableId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create EC2 SG
cliBlocks.content: $EC2_SG_ID = aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-s3-storage-ec2-sg --description "SSM-managed storage lab clients" --vpc-id $VPC_ID --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - create EFS SG
cliBlocks.content: $EFS_SG_ID = aws ec2 create-security-group --group-name fa-s3-storage-efs-sg --description "NFS only from storage lab clients" --vpc-id $VPC_ID --query GroupId --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - allow NFS from client SG
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id $EFS_SG_ID --protocol tcp --port 2049 --source-group $EC2_SG_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

tasks.title: Launch one SSM-managed EC2 storage client in each Availability Zone
tasks.goal: Launch fa-s3-storage-client-a and fa-s3-storage-client-b with no SSH key and the EFS/XFS packages installed by user data.
tasks.whyItMatters: The clients prove AZ-scoped EBS behavior and multi-AZ EFS shared access without opening inbound administrative ports.
tasks.examRelevance: EBS volumes attach within an Availability Zone; EFS is network file storage designed for concurrent clients.
warnings: The t3.micro clients and their public IPv4 addresses can incur charges while running.

browserSteps.instruction: Open EC2.
Launch fa-s3-storage-client-a using Amazon Linux 2023, t3.micro, subnet fa-s3-storage-public-a, fa-s3-storage-ec2-sg, no key pair and instance profile fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile.
Under Advanced details paste instance-user-data.sh.
Launch fa-s3-storage-client-b with the same settings except subnet fa-s3-storage-public-b.
Wait for both EC2 status checks to pass.
Open Systems Manager > Fleet Manager / Managed nodes and confirm both instances are managed.
Do not add SSH ingress.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - latest AL2023 AMI
cliBlocks.content: $AMI_ID = aws ssm get-parameter --name /aws/service/ami-amazon-linux-latest/al2023-ami-kernel-default-x86_64 --query Parameter.Value --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - launch client A
cliBlocks.content: $INSTANCE_A_ID = aws ec2 run-instances --image-id $AMI_ID --instance-type t3.micro --subnet-id $SUBNET_A_ID --security-group-ids $EC2_SG_ID --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile --associate-public-ip-address --user-data $USER_DATA_B64 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-client-a},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-s3-storage}]" --query "Instances[0].InstanceId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - launch client B
cliBlocks.content: $INSTANCE_B_ID = aws ec2 run-instances --image-id $AMI_ID --instance-type t3.micro --subnet-id $SUBNET_B_ID --security-group-ids $EC2_SG_ID --iam-instance-profile Name=fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile --associate-public-ip-address --user-data $USER_DATA_B64 --tag-specifications "ResourceType=instance,Tags=[{Key=Name,Value=fa-s3-storage-client-b},{Key=FollowAlong,Value=fa-s3-storage}]" --query "Instances[0].InstanceId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait for status checks
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 wait instance-status-ok --instance-ids $INSTANCE_A_ID $INSTANCE_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

tasks.title: Select an EBS volume type and create encrypted gp3 storage
tasks.goal: Use the EBS selection matrix, then create a 4-GiB encrypted gp3 volume in eu-west-2a and write a known file from client A.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exercise separates volume-family selection from encryption: all EBS volume types support encryption, while workload characteristics determine gp3/io2/st1/sc1 selection.
tasks.examRelevance: EBS is AZ-scoped block storage and gp3 is a strong general-purpose default for many workloads.

browserSteps.instruction: Open ebs-volume-types.json and review gp3, gp2, io2, io1, st1 and sc1.
Open EC2 > Volumes.
Choose Create volume.
Volume type: gp3.
Size: 4 GiB.
Availability Zone: eu-west-2a.
Encryption: enabled.
Use the account's default EBS KMS key.
Tag Name=fa-s3-storage-ebs-source and FollowAlong=fa-s3-storage.
Create the volume.
Select it, choose Actions > Attach volume, select fa-s3-storage-client-a and use device name /dev/sdf.
Use Systems Manager Run Command with prepare-ebs.sh.

prepare-ebs.sh
editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_SOURCE=$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /)
ROOT_PARENT=$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$ROOT_SOURCE" | head -n1)

DATA_DEV=$(lsblk -dpno NAME,TYPE | awk '$2=="disk"{print $1}' | grep -v "/dev/${ROOT_PARENT}" | head -n1)

if [ -z "${DATA_DEV}" ]; then
  echo "No non-root EBS data disk was detected."
  exit 1
fi

sudo mkfs.xfs -f "${DATA_DEV}"
sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ebs
sudo mount "${DATA_DEV}" /mnt/ebs

echo "fa-s3-storage encrypted EBS snapshot training file" | sudo tee /mnt/ebs/ebs-training.txt
sudo sync

sudo cat /mnt/ebs/ebs-training.txt
lsblk -f

expectedResults: The source volume is gp3, 4 GiB, eu-west-2a and Encrypted=true.
The training file exists on the XFS volume.

verificationChecks.text: KmsKeyId is populated.
The volume is attached only to client A in the same Availability Zone.

tasks.goal: Unmount/detach the source volume, create a snapshot, restore it to a second encrypted volume in eu-west-2a and prove the file survived.
tasks.whyItMatters: Snapshots are point-in-time backups; restoration creates a new EBS volume rather than mounting the snapshot directly as a normal filesystem.
tasks.examRelevance: Snapshots support backup/DR workflows and preserve encryption for encrypted source volumes.

browserSteps.instruction: Use SSM to run unmount-ebs.sh on client A.

Open the snapshot details and confirm Encrypted=true.
Create a new gp3 volume from the snapshot in eu-west-2a named fa-s3-storage-ebs-restored.
Confirm the restored volume is encrypted.
Attach it to client A as /dev/sdf.
Run verify-restored-ebs.sh through SSM.
Confirm the original training line is printed from the restored filesystem.

editableBlocks.content:
#!/bin/bash
set -euo pipefail

ROOT_SOURCE=$(findmnt -n -o SOURCE /)
ROOT_PARENT=$(lsblk -no PKNAME "$ROOT_SOURCE" | head -n1)

DATA_DEV=$(lsblk -dpno NAME,TYPE | awk '$2=="disk"{print $1}' | grep -v "/dev/${ROOT_PARENT}" | head -n1)

if [ -z "${DATA_DEV}" ]; then
  echo "No restored non-root EBS data disk was detected."
  exit 1
fi

sudo mkdir -p /mnt/ebs-restored
sudo mount -o ro "${DATA_DEV}" /mnt/ebs-restored
sudo cat /mnt/ebs-restored/ebs-training.txt

tasks.title: Review the SAA-C03 storage and backup decision points
tasks.goal: Summarize block/file/archive/hybrid storage and backup choices before teardown.
tasks.whyItMatters: The exam tests architecture selection: protocol, scope, performance, recovery time, cost and sharing behavior drive the answer.
tasks.examRelevance: The hands-on resources provide concrete anchors for EBS, EFS and Backup while the decision files cover expensive families safely.

browserSteps.instruction: EBS: AZ-scoped block storage for EC2; choose volume family based on latency, IOPS, throughput and cost.
EBS snapshots: point-in-time backups; restore by creating a new volume. Encrypted source volumes create encrypted snapshots.
EFS Regional: shared NFS file system with data stored across multiple AZs; mount targets provide VPC NFS endpoints.
EFS access point: application-specific root and POSIX identity boundary on the same file system.
FSx Windows: SMB/Active Directory.
FSx Lustre: high-performance parallel Linux/POSIX workloads and S3 integration.
FSx ONTAP: NetApp and multi-protocol NFS/SMB/iSCSI/NVMe requirements.
FSx OpenZFS: managed OpenZFS for NFS workloads.
AWS Backup plan: policy/schedule/lifecycle; backup selection: protected resources; recovery point: stored backup artifact.
Glacier Instant Retrieval: immediate access; Flexible/Deep Archive use restore workflows and different retrieval speeds.
Storage Gateway: hybrid file, block or virtual-tape interface to AWS storage.
Exam trigger: one EC2 database data disk -> EBS; multiple Linux hosts sharing the same files -> EFS.
Exam trigger: Windows SMB/AD -> FSx Windows; HPC + S3 dataset -> FSx Lustre.
Exam trigger: centrally scheduled multi-service backups -> AWS Backup.
Exam trigger: archive retrieval in minutes -> Flexible Retrieval Expedited; hours and lowest urgency -> Standard/Bulk or Deep Archive based on retention/retrieval need.

tasks.examRelevance: Safe cleanup is part of storage architecture because snapshots, EFS and backup recovery points continue accruing storage cost after compute stops.
warnings: Do not delete fa-s3-storage-vault until recovery points are gone. Do not delete EFS security groups until mount targets and client ENIs are gone.

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - capture recovery points
cliBlocks.content: $RECOVERY_POINTS = aws backup list-recovery-points-by-backup-vault --backup-vault-name fa-s3-storage-vault --query "RecoveryPoints[].RecoveryPointArn" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete recovery points
cliBlocks.content: foreach ($RP in ($RECOVERY_POINTS -split "\s+")) { if ($RP) { aws backup delete-recovery-point --backup-vault-name fa-s3-storage-vault --recovery-point-arn $RP --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin } }

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - delete backup vault
cliBlocks.content: aws backup delete-backup-vault --backup-vault-name fa-s3-storage-vault --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - unmount EFS on A
cliBlocks.content: $UNMOUNT_EFS = @{commands=@("sudo umount /mnt/efs || true")} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress; aws ssm send-command --instance-ids $INSTANCE_A_ID --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters $UNMOUNT_EFS --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - unmount EFS on B
cliBlocks.content: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids $INSTANCE_B_ID --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters $UNMOUNT_EFS --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait restored available
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 wait volume-available --volume-ids $EBS_RESTORED_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - wait clients terminated
cliBlocks.content: aws ec2 wait instance-terminated --instance-ids $INSTANCE_A_ID $INSTANCE_B_ID --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - route associations
cliBlocks.content: $ASSOCS = aws ec2 describe-route-tables --route-table-ids $RT_ID --query "RouteTables[0].Associations[?Main==`false`].RouteTableAssociationId" --output text --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin

cliBlocks.title: PowerShell - disassociate routes
cliBlocks.content: foreach ($A in ($ASSOCS -split "\s+")) { if ($A) { aws ec2 disassociate-route-table --association-id $A --region eu-west-2 --profile fa-s3-storage-admin } }

troubleshooting.title: EC2 clients do not appear in Systems Manager
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The instance profile, public egress route, public IPv4 address or SSM Agent startup is missing.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify fa-s3-storage-ec2-profile is attached, the subnet routes 0.0.0.0/0 to the IGW, and the instance has public IPv4 egress.

troubleshooting.title: prepare-ebs.sh reports no non-root disk
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The gp3 volume is not attached or the instance has not exposed the new NVMe block device yet.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify the EBS attachment is attached to client A, wait a few seconds, then rerun lsblk through SSM before rerunning the script.

troubleshooting.title: Restored EBS volume cannot attach
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The restored volume was created in an Availability Zone different from client A.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm both client A and fa-s3-storage-ebs-restored are in eu-west-2a; EBS attachment is AZ-scoped.

troubleshooting.title: EFS mount times out
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The EFS SG does not allow TCP 2049 from the EC2 SG or the mount target in that AZ is unavailable.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify fa-s3-storage-efs-sg inbound NFS source is fa-s3-storage-ec2-sg and one mount target is Available in each client AZ.

troubleshooting.title: EFS access-point mount fails because /shared does not exist
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Access-point root CreationInfo was omitted or incomplete.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify the access point contains /shared with OwnerUid=1001, OwnerGid=1001 and Permissions=0750.

troubleshooting.title: Client B cannot see the file written by client A
troubleshooting.likelyCause: One client mounted the file system root instead of the access point, the mount failed, or the write command did not complete.
troubleshooting.fix: Check mount output on both clients and confirm both use the same FILE_SYSTEM_ID and AP_ID.

troubleshooting.title: AWS Backup job fails immediately
troubleshooting.likelyCause: The backup role ARN/resource ARN is wrong or the service role lacks backup permissions.
troubleshooting.fix: Verify fa-s3-storage-backup-role has AWSBackupServiceRolePolicyForBackup and the selection/on-demand job references the exact EBS/EFS ARNs.

troubleshooting.title: Backup vault cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: One or more recovery points remain.
troubleshooting.fix: List recovery points in fa-s3-storage-vault and delete only those exact recovery points before retrying vault deletion.

troubleshooting.title: EFS security group cannot be deleted
troubleshooting.likelyCause: Mount-target ENIs or EC2 ENIs still reference the security groups.
troubleshooting.fix: Delete the access point/mount targets and terminate both clients before deleting the storage lab security groups.

warnings.cost: This lab creates two t3.micro EC2 clients with public IPv4 addresses, two 4-GiB EBS data volumes, one EBS snapshot, a small Regional EFS file system, two EFS mount targets, AWS Backup recovery points and a backup vault/plan. These can incur charges. FSx, Glacier archive objects and Storage Gateway appliances are intentionally not provisioned because their minimum capacities, minimum storage durations or gateway infrastructure can create disproportionate lab cost.
warnings.safety: Delete only exact fa-s3-storage resources and generated IDs derived from those names. Recovery points must be deleted before the backup vault; EFS mount targets before the EFS file system; EC2/EFS ENIs before security groups/VPC.
warnings.credentials: Never create root access keys and never place fa-s3-storage-admin credentials in user data, scripts, JSON plans, screenshots, chat or Study Tracker. Use only protected aws configure prompts.
